content:
Yesterday we saw how Israel witnessed the earth open and fire fall, and yet the very next morning they hardened their hearts and blamed Moses and Aaron. We may read this and wonder how a people could be so blind. But before we judge Israel too quickly, we must turn the light upon our own hearts, for the same hardness can grow in us. We live in a world in which the judgments of God are not hidden. We see this present evil world falling under the weight of its own sin. We see the kingdoms of men rise and fall. We see corruption exposed, nations shaken, families broken, and the fruit of sin ripening all around us. The Scripture had already declared, "The wages of sin is death" (Romans 6:23), and we watch that wage being paid before our eyes every day. And yet, like Israel, we can look upon all of it and remain strangely unmoved. Our hearts can grow hard even while we are surrounded by the clearest evidence of where sin leads.

Let us think about this very practically. We hear of a sudden death, and for a moment we are sobered, but by evening we have forgotten, and we go on living exactly as before, as though we ourselves will never die. Yet the Scripture says, "It is appointed for men to die once, but after this the judgment" (Hebrews 9:27). We see a marriage destroyed by unfaithfulness, and we grieve for a day, yet we still allow our own eyes to wander and our own hearts to flirt with the very thing that destroyed them. We watch a man ruined by dishonesty or greed, and we shake our heads, yet we continue in our own small dishonesties, telling ourselves that we are different. We see the misery that anger and bitterness bring into a home, and still we nurse our own resentments and refuse to forgive. This is the stone heart at work. It sees the judgment fall on others, and it feels a moment of fear, but it does not change. Like Israel, it witnesses the earth open, and by the next morning it is living as before.

The most fearful part of a hardened heart is that it happens slowly, and we do not feel it happening. No one decides in a single moment to become stone-hearted. It comes little by little. We hear a warning and delay. We feel conviction and push it aside. We know Yahweh is speaking, but we say,
"Not yet, not today." And each time we do this, the heart grows a little harder, a little less tender, a little slower to feel. The Scripture describes this drift, saying that some are "past feeling" (Ephesians 4:19), and it warns that people can have "their own conscience seared with a hot iron" (1 Timothy 4:2). A conscience is like skin; when it is burned again and again, it stops feeling pain. And this is the danger for the New Creation. We can hear the truth so often, and resist it so often, that eventually the truth no longer moves us. The very familiarity of the warning becomes the reason we ignore it. We have heard it before, and so we no longer tremble at it.

There is another way our hearts grow hard, and it is exactly the way Israel's did. When judgment or difficulty comes, we look for someone to blame.

Israel blamed Moses and Aaron for the deaths that their own rebellion had caused. And we do the same. When the consequences of our choices catch up with us, we blame our circumstances, our family, our upbringing, the church, the leaders, or even God Himself. Adam blamed Eve, and Eve blamed the serpent (Genesis 3:12-13), and ever since, the hard heart has always looked outward for someone to accuse rather than inward in repentance. As long as we are blaming others, we will never repent, because repentance requires us to say, "I have sinned," and the stone heart will say anything except those three words. The soft heart says with David, "Against You, you only, have I sinned" (Psalm 51:4). The hard heart blames others.

But here is the good news, and it is very precious. Yahweh is able to give a new heart. He is not only the Judge whose fire fell upon the rebellion; He is also the merciful God who promises, "I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh and give you a heart of flesh" (Ezekiel 36:26). What we cannot do for ourselves, Yahweh can do for us. We cannot soften our own hearts by our own strength, but we can come to Him and ask Him to do it. And this is why the Scripture presses upon us that little word today. It does not say tomorrow. It does not say someday. It says, "Today, if you will hear His voice, do not harden your hearts" (Hebrews 3:15). Every time we hear Yahweh's voice and obey it quickly, the heart stays tender. Every time we hear and delay, the heart grows a little harder. So the safest thing the New Creation can ever do is to respond to Yahweh at once, while the heart is still soft enough to feel.

So let us examine ourselves honestly. Are we seeing the judgments of God in this world and remaining unmoved? Are we hearing the same warnings again and again without changing? Are we quicker to blame others than to repent ourselves? Are there convictions we have pushed aside so many times that we no longer feel them? If so, let us not wait until the heart is past feeling. Let us come to Yahweh now, while His voice still stirs us, and pray, "Take out this heart of stone, and give me a heart of flesh." Israel saw the earth open and hardened their hearts by the next morning. May it not be so with us. May we be a people who see the hand of God, tremble, repent, and soften, rather than a people who see everything and are changed by nothing. Let us keep our hearts tender before Yahweh, quick to hear, quick to obey, and quick to repent, so that the stone heart of Israel never becomes our own.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God, who alone can turn a heart of stone into a heart of flesh,
We confess that we can see Your judgments in the world and still remain unmoved.

Forgive us for hearing the same warnings again and again without changing.

Keep us from blaming others when we ought to fall down and say, 'I have sinned.'

Do not let us push aside conviction until we can no longer feel it.

Take the stone out of our hearts, and give us tender hearts that respond to You today.

"I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you."

Ezekiel 36:26
In Christ name we pray. Amen.
